## Example 5.4 {#ss5-example-5-4 .gp-lesson}

It is given that $x-3$, $x$ and $x+12$ form a geometric sequence. Find:

::: {.gp-subparts}
a) the value of $x$;

b) the common ratio for this sequence
:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 31 · Example 5.4</p>

::: notes

With non-zero terms, x/(x−3)=(x+12)/x. Thus x²=(x−3)(x+12)=x²+9x−36, so x=4. This satisfies the required denominator restrictions x≠0,3. The terms are 1,4,16 and r=4. Encourage students to verify both ratios after solving. Do not insert the ratio equation on the student slide before they translate the question themselves.

:::
